- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of the 30d window).
- Forecasts show upward momentum bias, often peaking too early and then plateauing or declining — suggesting failure to capture mean reversion or volatility decay.
- After sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 35.63, 38.18), forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward — indicating poor lag response to recent highs.
- Model underestimates volatility in the middle-to-late period of the 30d window, particularly when true values show sharp drops or erratic swings.
- Forecasts tend to smooth out noise, suppressing short-term volatility, which leads to underestimation of true price swings.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical mean is below 35 — suggesting calibration issue with baseline or trend assumptions.
- Forecasts often fail to adjust for seasonal or event-driven corrections (e.g., policy changes, emissions caps) — leading to persistent overestimation in high-activity periods.
- Model does not adequately account for “rebound” or “reversion” after sharp declines — underestimates the likelihood of a quick recovery or correction.
